classification.difficultyReason: Combines component quantities from different mixture ratios and reverses the given ratio order in part c.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Two containers each contain 1 L of orange cordial. The first container contains cordial concentrate and water in the ratio $1:9$, and the second container contains cordial concentrate and water in the ratio $1:8$. The contents of both containers are tipped into a 2-litre bottle. What is the ratio of cordial concentrate to water in the 2-litre bottle?

answer.short:
$19:161$

Find the concentrate and water volumes in each container, then add matching components.
answer.worked:
Each first-container part is $\frac{1}{10}$ L; each second-container part is $\frac{1}{9}$ L.

$$\begin{align*}\text{First concentrate volume}&=\frac{1}{10}\text{ L}\\\text{First water volume}&=\frac{9}{10}\text{ L}\\\text{Second concentrate volume}&=\frac{1}{9}\text{ L}\\\text{Second water volume}&=\frac{8}{9}\text{ L}\\\text{Total concentrate volume}&=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{9}=\frac{19}{90}\text{ L}\\\text{Total water volume}&=\frac{9}{10}+\frac{8}{9}=\frac{161}{90}\text{ L}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=\frac{19}{90}:\frac{161}{90}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=19:161\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: A bottle contains 1 L of cordial. The ratio of cordial concentrate to water is $1:5$. Another bottle contains 0.5 L of cordial. The ratio of cordial concentrate to water in this bottle is $1:4$. The contents of both bottles are tipped into a third container. What is the ratio of cordial concentrate to water in this third container?

answer.short:
$8:37$

Divide each bottle's volume into its ratio parts before combining the components.
answer.worked:
The first bottle has $1+5=6$ parts; the second has $1+4=5$ parts.

$$\begin{align*}\text{First concentrate volume}&=1\div6=\frac16\text{ L}\\\text{First water volume}&=5\times\frac16=\frac56\text{ L}\\\text{Second concentrate volume}&=\frac12\div5=\frac1{10}\text{ L}\\\text{Second water volume}&=4\times\frac1{10}=\frac25\text{ L}\\\text{Total concentrate volume}&=\frac16+\frac1{10}=\frac4{15}\text{ L}\\\text{Total water volume}&=\frac56+\frac25=\frac{37}{30}\text{ L}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=\frac4{15}:\frac{37}{30}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=8:37\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: A bottle contains one-third of a litre of cordial, which consists of water and cordial concentrate in the ratio $1:4$. Two-thirds of a litre of water are then poured in. What is the ratio of concentrate to water now?

answer.short:
$4:11$

The given ratio is water to concentrate; give the final ratio in the requested reverse order.
answer.worked:
The original cordial has $1+4=5$ parts.

$$\begin{align*}\text{One part}&=\frac13\div5=\frac1{15}\text{ L}\\\text{Concentrate volume}&=4\times\frac1{15}=\frac4{15}\text{ L}\\\text{Original water volume}&=\frac1{15}\text{ L}\\\text{Final water volume}&=\frac1{15}+\frac23=\frac{11}{15}\text{ L}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=\frac4{15}:\frac{11}{15}\\\text{Concentrate:water}&=4:11\end{align*}$$
